summary: Action plugins combine local processing with module functionality; subclass ActionBase as ActionModule and call _execute_module to run the underlying module, then modify its return data.
questions: How do I write an action plugin that wraps a module?
How does an action plugin call the real module?
When should I use an action plugin?

answer_card.title: Action plugin basics
answer_card.answer_md:
```python
from ansible.plugins.action import ActionBase

class ActionModule(ActionBase):
    def run(self, tmp=None, task_vars=None):
        module_return = self._execute_module(module_name='<NAME_OF_MODULE>',
                                             module_args=module_args,
                                             task_vars=task_vars, tmp=tmp)
```
Action plugins run on the control node, letting you mix local data/processing with a module and post-process its result.
